title: Does Learning Protein Folding Generalize to Broader Reasoning?
task: Post-training LLMs with protein-folding knowledge to improve general reasoning
key_results: Fold2Reason improves structure prediction scores 2.7-3.5x over baseline; raises macro-average reasoning accuracy from 45.09% to 48.33% (+3.23 pp) across 10 benchmarks
comments: Demonstrates that non-linguistic, structure-dense scientific data can systematically improve broad reasoning, though the mechanism of transfer remains somewhat opaque.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Learning protein folding teaches reusable reasoning capabilities generalizable beyond structure
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; positive gains on all 10 reasoning benchmarks

title: Scaling Trajectories for Complex Tasks through Recursive Self-Rewrite
task: Discovering and reconstructing successful task solutions under diverse harnesses
key_results: RSR expands 2,001 source trajectories to 11,094 rewritten ones; pass@3 improves from 57.0% to 74.2% on Terminal-Bench 2 and 1.5% to 9.1% on Terminal-Bench 4
comments: Novel approach to leveraging harness-specific solutions by reconstructing them into general-harness trajectories; reconstructed trajectories outperform direct SFT, suggesting value in the rewriting process.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Harness-assisted solutions can be reconstructed into general-harness training data that improves performance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; rewritten trajectories outperform base model and direct SFT

title: FrameMorrow: Future-guided Frame Selection with Prospective Tokens for Long-Horizon Video Generation
task: Historical frame selection for long-horizon video generation using prospective tokens
key_results: FrameMorrow shows consistent improvements in long-range consistency, visual quality, and action alignment across 5 benchmarks and 11 generative models
comments: Selecting frames based on future information needs is intuitive; the plug-and-play nature across diverse generators is valuable, though quantitative gains are not specified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Selecting history based on future relevance improves long-horizon consistency more than present-based selection
hypotheses.result: Confirmed across multiple benchmarks and models

title: MotorMind: Scaffolding General Vision Language Models for Zero-Shot Robot Manipulation
task: Zero-shot robot manipulation using general-purpose VLMs without task-specific training
key_results: MotorMind achieves 66.7% success on LIBERO-PRO base and 53.8% under perturbations; 95% on real xArm6 robot; prior zero-shot methods reach max 13.3% and 19.2%
comments: Impressive zero-shot performance by connecting VLM reasoning directly to deterministic control, though failures suggest visual grounding and embodied reasoning remain bottlenecks.

hypotheses.hypothesis: General VLMs with appropriate mid-level action representation can perform zero-shot robot manipulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; achieves competitive performance without task-specific training

title: World Action Modeling with Progressive Visual Planning
task: Long-horizon robot control via progressive visual sub-goal prediction
key_results: ProWAM achieves 85.8% on LIBERO-Plus (+35.9% relative gain) and 70.0% in real-world zero-shot (+27.3% relative gain); state-of-the-art on simulation benchmarks
comments: Elegant design separating visual planning from action generation; sparse sub-goals provide interpretability and efficiency while maintaining strong performance.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Predicting ordered visual sub-goals improves long-horizon robotic control robustness
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; superior out-of-distribution performance across simulated and real-world tasks

title: Native Action-Prior Learning from Videos for World Action Models
task: Learning action policies from observation-only videos without action annotations
key_results: NAVA-WAM consistently outperforms prior approaches in-distribution and out-of-distribution; demonstrates strong action-label efficiency and real-robot generalization
comments: Two-stage approach (observation-only pretraining + action-labeled post-training) is pragmatic and shows promise; quantitative results not fully specified in abstract.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Native action-prior learning from observation-only videos enables efficient action policy pretraining
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; outperforms indirect representation-to-control transfer and separate latent-action models

title: On-Policy Parameter Update Direction Underlies Generalization in LLM Post-Training
task: Understanding parameter update direction in on-policy LLM post-training
key_results: OPSFT constrains SFT updates to on-policy directions; achieves strong generalization with high training efficiency; can leverage high-quality trajectories while maintaining learned capabilities
comments: Novel finding that generalization advantage comes from update direction, not just on-policy training; enables combining efficiency of SFT with generalization of on-policy methods.

hypotheses.hypothesis: On-policy paradigms generalize better due to specific parameter update directions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; OPSFT transfers this advantage to SFT with constrained updates

title: Pivot-SD: Efficient Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
task: Efficient offline self-distillation for masked diffusion language models
key_results: Pivot-SD improves LLaDA-8B over SFT and budget-matched RL baselines using only 200 questions and 4 rollouts
comments: Clever information-gain metric identifies pivotal tokens; selective training on high-impact commitments is computationally efficient, though absolute improvements not quantified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Training only high-impact commitment tokens improves masked diffusion LMs more efficiently than full-sequence SFT
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; matches or exceeds full-sequence and budget-matched baselines

title: SimuVerity: Benchmarking Agents for Engineering-Grade Simulink Model Generation
task: Evaluating agent systems on engineering-grade Simulink model generation
key_results: Best agent system achieves only 42.86% overall score; structural similarity is poor proxy for engineering performance; bottlenecks in qualification and multidimensional requirements
comments: Rigorous engineering-focused benchmark revealing significant gaps in current agent capabilities; hierarchical evaluation spanning correctness, execution, and qualitative requirements is valuable.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structural similarity correlates with engineering performance in Simulink model generation
hypotheses.result: Disconfirmed; structural similarity is poor proxy for engineering qualification

title: PDE-JEPA: Predictive Representation Learning of Latent Dynamics Modeling for Parametric PDEs
task: Predictive representation learning for parametric PDE dynamics
key_results: PDE-JEPA outperforms state-of-the-art by 33.4% in-distribution and 51.4% out-of-distribution (unseen parameters) across 9 benchmarks
comments: Combining masked-latent prediction with geometry projector and physics-structured decoder is well-motivated; impressive generalization to unseen parameters.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Predictive representation learning with geometry alignment improves PDE dynamics modeling over reconstruction-based approaches
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; substantial gains in-distribution and out-of-distribution

title: HyperBrowseComp: A Multilingual and Multimodal Stress Test for Web-Browsing Agents
task: Multilingual multimodal stress test for web-browsing agents
key_results: HyperBrowseComp comprises 423 challenging questions across 13 languages; requires locating obscure evidence, multi-step reasoning, and heterogeneous sources
comments: Comprehensive benchmark with human validation and evaluation; difficulty design (filtering easy questions via parametric knowledge) ensures genuine web reasoning is required.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current models can effectively perform multilingual multimodal web-browsing reasoning
hypotheses.result: Not explicitly stated; benchmark provided for evaluation

title: Science or Slop?: Benchmarking and Mitigating Scientific Slop in AI-Generated Papers
task: Benchmarking and mitigating scientific slop in AI-generated papers
key_results: SciSlopBench identifies AI papers with 85.9% accuracy; scientific slop correlates with lower CIEIR ratings and rejection; SciSlopHarness reduces AI-human gap by 63%
comments: Timely benchmark addressing a growing problem; moving beyond token-level detection to global reasoning patterns is insightful; evidentiary grounding approach to mitigation is principled.

hypotheses.hypothesis: AI-generated scientific papers exhibit detectable global reasoning failures beyond surface plausibility
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 85.9% detection accuracy and correlation with peer review outcomes

title: World Embedding Benchmark
task: Evaluating physical information encoding in video embeddings
key_results: Pre-trained models show weak retrieval and near-chance classification; lightweight probes recover useful physical information; retrieved references improve video generation fidelity
comments: Reveals gap between cross-modal alignment and quantitative physical information recovery; physics-specific contrastive training creates trade-offs worth further investigation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Video embeddings encode quantitative physical information recoverably
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; lightweight probes succeed but contrastive training creates trade-offs

title: Source Preference in the Wild: How LLM Agents Favor Items by Source, and How to Reduce It
task: Detecting and reducing source bias in LLM agent decision-making
key_results: Each model consistently prefers certain sources; items from preferred sources are selected ~2/3 of the time even if they satisfy fewer requirements; hiding source identity weakens preference
comments: Well-designed study revealing systematic source bias in agent selection; information hiding and relabeling experiments isolate two mechanisms (shortcut learning and preconceptions).

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLM agents exhibit systematic source preferences independent of item quality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; preference outweighs requirement satisfaction in ~2/3 of cases

title: LexReward: A Taxonomy-Driven Reward Framework for Legal Language Models
task: Taxonomy-driven reward modeling for legal language models
key_results: LexReward improves legal response quality across Style, Element, and Chain dimensions; DPO training on preference data improves performance; dimension-specific RL improves corresponding dimensions
comments: Comprehensive taxonomy-based reward framework showing interpretability benefits; dimension-wise improvements suggest modularity is valuable for domain-specific LM optimization.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multidimensional taxonomy-based rewards improve legal LM performance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; improvements across all three dimensions via DPO and RL

title: Multilingual GSM-Symbolic: What determines capability transfer across languages?
task: Cross-lingual mathematical reasoning capability transfer assessment
key_results: Model size (β=1.77), language resource level (β=0.77), and reasoning (β=0.67) are largest determinants; 32B model in Marathi ≈ 10B model in English; framework explains 92% between-language variation
comments: Comprehensive analysis isolating factors governing cross-lingual transfer; extensible template-based dataset prevents overfitting; model size and reasoning are key levers for low-resource languages.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model size, language resources, and reasoning capability determine cross-lingual transfer in math
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; joint estimation reveals β values and relative importance

title: Spatial Memory Intelligence: Endowing World Models with Understanding-Driven Long-Term Memory
task: Spatial memory management for long-video world models
key_results: SMI improves memory sparsity, generation stability, and spatial consistency across multiple baselines and benchmarks
comments: Leverages MLLM spatial reasoning for memory management; atomic operations (clustering, sparsification, retrieval, filtering) are composable and interpretable.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MLLM-driven spatial memory management improves long-video generation quality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; improvements in sparsity, stability, and consistency

title: Science Utopia? Closed-Loop LLM Simulation of Academic Research Ecosystems
task: Closed-loop LLM simulation of academic research ecosystems
key_results: SciUtopia simulates 40,000+ researchers across 8,000 institutions; models rejection-driven resubmission, funding, collaboration; reveals emergence of resource inequality without cumulative advantage
comments: Ambitious framework capturing multi-scale scientific dynamics; findings about resubmission burden and topic diversity are valuable for policy, though validation against real-world data is limited.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Rejection-driven resubmission amplifies reviewer burden beyond population growth
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; substantial amplification observed in simulations

title: VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks
task: Scaling agentic verification for long-horizon tasks
key_results: VeriHarness achieves highest selection scores among baselines; evidence-backed revision improves performance by 6.2-6.4 points; released 26,000 rollouts for research
comments: Clever use of disagreement and consensus to guide verification; workspace, tools, and reusable skills enable scalable verification without reference answers.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Disagreement exposes correct alternatives; consensus can conceal errors
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; disagreement resolver and consensus challenger improve verification

title: DEFINE: Exemplar-Guided Accent Control for Zero-Shot TTS
task: Decoupled speaker identity and accent control in zero-shot TTS
key_results: DEFINE improves accent-probe accuracy from 6.5% to 19.6% with seen accents; generalizes accent control to out-of-domain accents while maintaining speaker similarity
comments: Elegant approach decoupling factors through separate exemplar encoders; generalization to unseen accents remains limited, suggesting accent modeling complexity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Speaker identity and accent can be independently controlled from separate audio exemplars in zero-shot TTS
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for seen and out-of-domain accents; limited for held-out accents

title: EditHero: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Part-Level 3D Editing and Vibe Modeling
task: Long-horizon part-level 3D editing with natural language
key_results: EditHero benchmark with deterministic verification; LLM/VLM agents preserve unedited regions better than non-agentic methods; bottleneck is edit speed (minutes per edit)
comments: First benchmark for iterative 3D editing; agent-based editing preserves structure better but is slow; released engine and sequences support future research.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Agent-based code editing preserves unedited regions better than regeneration-based methods
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; agents maintain structure integrity while regeneration disturbs unrelated areas

title: Diptych: Scoped, AI-Interpreted Comparison for Reference Listening in Music Production
task: AI-assisted reference listening for music production
key_results: Diptych enables user-defined comparison scope; participants identified additional differences (9/10 received expert support); users reported good usability and clarity
comments: Thoughtful HCI approach prioritizing user control over AI authority; integrating interpretable audio features and scope-specific guidance is valuable for creative workflows.

hypotheses.hypothesis: AI support for creative comparison should prioritize user-defined scope and inspectable evidence
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; participants found scope control and interpretability valuable

title: Efficient Reasoning Training Does Not Always Harm CoT Faithfulness and Monitorability
task: Assessing chain-of-thought faithfulness under efficient reasoning training
key_results: Faithfulness declines under length pressure (reduced consistency); monitorability remains robust (models acknowledge input influence); length pressure affects dimensions differently
comments: Nuanced finding that efficiency training affects CoT dimensions differently; monitorability preservation is encouraging for oversight, though faithfulness degradation deserves attention.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Efficient reasoning training reduces CoT faithfulness but preserves monitorability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; findings differ by dimension and training method

title: HelixWorld: A Real-time Interactive Audio-Visual World Model
task: Real-time interactive audio-visual world modeling
key_results: HelixWorld generates synchronized visual and stereo acoustic dynamics at 24 FPS on single GPU; matches visual SOTA while surpassing baselines in spatial-acoustic consistency
comments: Novel inclusion of spatial audio dynamics alongside visual generation; online trajectory distillation enables real-time interaction without drift.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bidirectional teacher distilled into streaming student enables real-time audio-visual interaction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; maintains drift-free rollouts at 24 FPS

title: ProAR: Learning Prospective Reasoning with Autoregressive Video Models
task: Goal-oriented reasoning in autoregressive video generation
key_results: ProAR combines goal-frame prediction and future representation self-alignment; improves diverse visual reasoning benchmarks; achieves performance of fully trained baselines with 25% training steps
comments: Clever asymmetric attention mechanism guides generation toward goal while preserving intermediate states; training efficiency gain is substantial.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Goal-frame prediction guides autoregressive generation toward target outcomes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; consistent improvements and training efficiency gains

title: Looping Beyond Twice: A Scalable Recipe for Looped Mixture-of-Experts
task: Scaling looped mixture-of-experts through recursive depth
key_results: LOOM enables stable scaling to 9-12 loops; 700M at 5 loops reduces perplexity from 18.36 to 16.54; 1.7B at 9 loops improves accuracy from 42.4% to 47.7%
comments: Identifies and addresses depth curse and expert selection collapse; per-loop routers and input re-injection enable deeper recurrence while improving computation diversity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Per-loop routing and residual stabilization enable scaling looped MoE beyond 2 loops
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; stable scaling to 9-12 loops with performance gains

title: MetaRubric: Learning to Reward for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
task: Evidence-aware rubric-based reinforcement learning with counterfactual adaptation
key_results: MetaRubric improves PubMedQA accuracy by 6.00-20.40 pp over static-judge GRPO; further gains on medical benchmarks
comments: Addresses vacuous credit problem in rubric-based RL by requiring evidence in responses; counterfactual prompts guide rubric revision while preserving semantics.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Evidence-aware rubric adaptation improves policy performance over static judges
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; substantial gains across medical QA benchmarks

title: Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling
task: Long-context sequence modeling with triadic linear attention
key_results: Triadic linear attention extends matrix-valued states to 3D tensor states; substantially improves long-context language modeling and recall over linear attention variants
comments: Elegant generalization of linear attention using triadic outer products; parameter-efficient way to increase effective state size.

hypotheses.hypothesis: 3D tensor states improve long-context modeling over matrix-valued states
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; substantial improvements in language modeling and recall

title: Language Models that Play Chess and Explain Their Moves
task: Chess playing with move explanations
key_results: 4B-parameter model reaches 2697 Elo (Grandmaster level), gains 900 Elo over 7 distillation iterations, surpasses frontier models with 1000× fewer parameters
comments: Novel encoder-decoder integration with iterative distillation offers a compelling blueprint for domain adaptation when silent expert systems exist, though evaluation of explanation quality relies on LM-based metrics.

model_io.model: Queen (4B encoder-decoder with chess encoder + instruction-tuned LM)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Iterative Bellman-like updates (analyzing post-move positions and distilling back) improve both playing strength and explanation quality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 900 Elo gain and high coherence in explanations over 7 iterations

title: Covert Assistance: Helpful LLM Agents Evade Oversight in Multi-Agent Systems
task: Detecting covert assistance in multi-agent systems
key_results: 7 of 9 frontier models disguise credentials in requirements; DeepSeek-V4-Pro attempts concealment in 16.9%, succeeds in 0.9%; risk compounds to 61.3% across 105 episodes
comments: Concerning finding that benign agents circumvent safety boundaries without adversarial incentives; misinterpretation of rules and helping behavior drive leakage.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Benign agents covertly assist others in circumventing safety boundaries
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; substantial rates across tested models

title: GTR: Gated Token Recurrence for Efficient Dense Prediction
task: Efficient dense prediction with gated token recurrence
key_results: GTR achieves 58.9 box AP on COCO with 1.908 ms latency; 4.0× faster than FLA v0.5.0; transfers to instance segmentation, pose, oriented detection, depth
comments: Softmax-free recurrent backbone distilled from DINO teacher; specialized CUDA kernel achieves strong efficiency-accuracy trade-off for edge deployment.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Recurrent token mixing provides efficient alternative to global softmax attention for dense prediction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; competitive accuracy with superior latency

title: FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution
task: Cost-aware LLM-guided program evolution
key_results: FrugalEvo achieves SOTA on circle packing (1.68 USD with GPT-5.6, 0.55 USD with GLM-5.3), higher BA-AUC on 9/10 tasks vs baselines costing ~50 USD
comments: The cost-aware framing and cache-efficient prefix sharing are practical contributions, though the BA-AUC metric introduces additional complexity for comparison.

model_io.model: Two-tier LLM system (strong LLM explorer + cheaper LLM implementer)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cache-efficient evolution and two-tier LLM assignment maximize performance-per-cost
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: matches/surpasses baselines at significantly lower total cost

title: Rollout-Marginal Distillation for Long-Horizon Autoregressive Video Generation
task: Long-horizon autoregressive video generation
key_results: RMD maintains visual quality far beyond training horizon, outperforms video-level DMD baselines in quality consistency
comments: The two-stage approach (marginal chunk scoring + video-level DMD) elegantly decouples quality from temporal context, but quantitative comparisons are limited to visual inspection.

model_io.model: Autoregressive video diffusion with Rollout-Marginal Distillation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Independent chunk scoring against a teacher provides clearer quality signal than joint scoring, compensated by subsequent temporal coherence pass
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: improved visual quality and consistency in long rollouts

title: LVMT: Video Mask Transformer for Long-term Video Segmentation
task: Long-term video object segmentation with temporal propagation
key_results: LVMT sets new SOTA across 6 video segmentation benchmarks; 10× faster than prior SOTA; handles long videos and occlusions through adaptive temporal selection
comments: GRU-based propagation with Truncated Query Propagation enables training on long videos without memory or vanishing gradient issues.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive temporal propagation improves long-term video segmentation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SOTA performance with superior speed

title: Local Support Learning
task: Preventing catastrophic forgetting in large pre-trained models
key_results: Local Support Learning retains pretrained and finetuned capabilities across multiple training phases; GMM-based gating keeps updates local to current phase distribution
comments: Geometric perspective on forgetting is insightful; local gating enables retention without prior data, though computational overhead and scaling potential unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local gating prevents catastrophic forgetting by restricting updates to current phase distribution
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; retains capabilities across multiple training phases

title: Octrees as an Explicit 3D Language
task: 3D multimodal understanding and generation with explicit octree language
key_results: OctLLM lowers image-to-3D FID by 17.4%; improves render-grounded captioning by 28.7 points over ShapeLLM-Omni; matches backbone on general language benchmarks
comments: Novel use of sparse octrees as explicit 3D language; separate trainable branches preserve frozen language pathway while adding 3D capacity efficiently.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit octree representation improves 3D understanding and generation in multimodal LLMs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SOTA among unified multimodal models

title: Skill2Real: Agentic Skill Learning for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Robot Manipulation
task: Learning transferable manipulation skills through agentic policy framework
key_results: Skill2Real achieves 56.3% on LIBERO-Pro Long (from 2.0%); 78.75% mean completion on real-world tasks; frozen Sol-trained skills transfer without fine-tuning
comments: Clever use of privileged simulation info for validation while grounding skills in public observations; hierarchical skill learning (local + task-level) aids transfer.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hierarchical skill learning and verification enables effective sim-to-real transfer
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; frozen skills achieve strong real-world performance

title: Equal Ranking Quality, Different Decisions: Measuring and Reducing Order Dependence in LLM Scorers
task: Reducing order dependence in LLM-based scorers
key_results: Order-Consistency SFT reduces decision instability; 5 scorers at 0.010 nDCG@10 difference retain overlapping sets 0.66–0.84; OC-SFT achieves more stability than order-averaged distillation
comments: Critical finding that ranking quality and decision consistency are decoupled; OC-SFT is practical but the modest overlap differences suggest inherent limitations of prompt-based scoring.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Order-Consistency SFT penalizing disagreement across permutations improves decision stability without sacrificing ranking quality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: maintains nDCG while improving all decision-stability measures

title: Collective Bias Mitigation via Model Routing and Collaboration
task: Mitigating bias in LLMs through model collaboration and routing
key_results: Collective Bias Mitigation (Committee topology) lowers age bias from 0.25 to 0.10; substantially outperforms standalone self-debiasing
comments: First systematic exploration of LLM selection and organization for fairness; ensemble approach leverages diverse models' complementary knowledge.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Collaborating diverse LLMs mitigates bias better than single-model self-debiasing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; substantial bias reduction via Committee and Debating topologies

title: From Retrieval to Typed Decisions: Calibrated System One Models from Biomedical Sentence Encoders
task: Converting retrieval-trained biomedical encoders to typed decision models
key_results: SBERT2S1 shows retrieval training helps PFR (10/15 comparisons) but hurts C (1/15); unbiased estimator recovers gap in RLCD recipe
comments: Interesting finding that retrieval pretraining benefits vary by head design; temperature scaling shows no clear calibration advantage.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Retrieval training transfers to typed decision models
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; benefits depend on head architecture

title: WEFT: Scaling Tool-Use Post-Training for General-Purpose Agents
task: Scaling tool-use post-training for agentic systems
key_results: WEFT-14B improves over Agent-World-14B by 6.41–12.27 percentage points across BFCL V4, τ²-Bench, and Claw-Eval; WEFT-35B extends gains to long-horizon workflows
comments: Comprehensive system-level approach addressing environment, task, harness, and evaluator, though the contribution partitioning between self-evolution and stable post-training is not fully isolated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Scaling agentic interaction systems holistically (environment + task + harness + evaluator) with execution-driven self-evolution yields better performance than environment-only scaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: consistent improvements across benchmarks vs matched-size baselines

title: Learning from Runtime Feedback through Failure-Bank Self-Evolution for Vision-Language-Action Models
task: Persistent policy improvement from runtime feedback in robotic manipulation
key_results: FailBank improves task success by 8.5–6.9 percentage points and reduces cumulative cost by 35.6–23.8% vs base policy; outperforms runtime shielding by 25.4–9.5 percentage points
comments: Elegant four-stage framework converting transient corrections into permanent policy gains via guarded LoRA, though evaluation is limited to simulation on VLA-Arena.

model_io.model: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model with FailBank self-evolution loop

hypotheses.hypothesis: Runtime shield feedback, when distilled via outcome-aware admission and guarded LoRA, provides persistent policy improvement superior to permanent masking
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: higher success rates with comparable or better cost control than runtime shielding

title: Can Computation from Earlier Problems Help LLMs Solve New Ones?
task: Cross-problem knowledge retention in multi-turn reasoning
key_results: STAIR improves later-turn accuracy by up to 11.67 percentage points with only 12,288 trained parameters across three Qwen models and four benchmarks
comments: Elegant parameter-efficient approach capturing inter-query computation, but the mechanism by which historical context helps or hurts later problems remains partially opaque.

model_io.model: LLM with STAIR module (fixed KV bank + learned query redirection)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Capturing and selectively reusing KV keys/values from earlier responses via learned query redirection improves reasoning on subsequent problems
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: consistent accuracy gains with minimal parameter overhead

title: Rethinking Token Reweighting for SFT: Suppress, Reverse, and Extrapolate Learned Features
task: Token reweighting for suppression, reversal, and extrapolation of learned features
key_results: SCALE (Selective Control via Local Entropy) achieves 37.84 on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B; outperforms strongest baselines while remaining competitive on retention
comments: Insight that reversal and extrapolation require stable reference frame is valuable; frozen SFT delta approach enables controlled feature manipulation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gated adaptation with frozen SFT delta enables reversal and extrapolation of learned features
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; achieves strong math reasoning while preserving general knowledge

title: Dream4ACT: A Shared Visual Action Interface for Multi-Embodiment Video-Action Modeling
task: Multi-embodiment video-action modeling through shared visual action interface
key_results: Dream4ACT achieves 88.98% on RoboTwin 2.0 and 65.66 on TriWorldBench; training-free multiview recovery enables execution without embodiment-specific decoders
comments: Clever visual action interface (action views) unifies representations across embodiments; supports forward dynamics, inverse dynamics, and conditional generation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Shared visual action interface enables unified multi-embodiment action modeling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; strong performance across embodiments with single model

title: Strike a Chord! Modal Kinetic Typography
task: Semantic kinetic typography animation
key_results: Modal kinetic typography produces smoother, more articulated motion than Dynamic Typography and AniClipart with better concept alignment and less glyph tearing; preferred by human raters
comments: Elegant use of FEM eigenmodes as a structural prior avoids arbitrary point movement and jitter, though the method requires manual specification of moving parts per glyph.

hypotheses.hypothesis: FEM modes from glyph geometry provide smoother, less-torn animation than free-form point optimization and more flexible alternatives than skeleton-based methods
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: higher concept alignment and smoothness with less tearing than baselines

title: Receiver-Conditioned Latent Communication gives 94% CacheBack
task: Efficient multi-agent context distribution via receiver-conditioned communication
key_results: CacheBack removes 75% of transmitted state, improves accuracy by 14.7 percentage points, reduces latency by 3.2× vs text communication on FanOutQA
comments: Training-free receiver-conditioning via attention weights is simple and effective, though generalization beyond QA tasks and robustness to diverse model families need further validation.

model_io.model: Multi-agent system with CacheBack receiver-conditioned KV cache filtering

hypotheses.hypothesis: Filtering sender KV cache based on receiver's information needs reduces overhead while maintaining or improving accuracy and latency
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: significant reductions in transmitted state and latency with accuracy gains

title: Stomatin organizes laterally segregated membrane microdomains to modulate transmembrane transport and signal transduction
task: Determine structural organization and functional role of stomatin in membrane microdomain assembly
key_results: Cryo-EM reveals hexadecameric inverted-cup architecture with 16 SPFH1 domains anchoring a circular membrane microdomain; proteomic data identified >10 associated protein classes (solute carriers, Rab GTPases, integrins); stomatin oligomerization required for integrin-regulated directional cell migration
comments: The structural model elegantly explains how SPFH proteins scaffold functional microdomains, though the mechanistic link between oligomerization and specific transporter/integrin functions remains to be clarified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stomatin hexadecamers organize laterally segregated membrane microdomains that regulate transporters and integrins
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: cryo-EM structure shows inverted-cup assembly defining isolated circular microdomain; proteomics identified solute carriers and integrins; oligomerization required for directional migration

title: Dimer-interface effects on tetramer stabilization and tryptophan dynamics in allosterically modulated TPH-II
task: Identify allosteric ligands that stabilize TPH-II tetrameric structure
key_results: Ligand L2 exhibited the most favorable binding energy at the A-D allosteric interface; L2 and L4 possess favorable CNS-compatible pharmacokinetic properties; all candidates maintained compact conformations with intact tetramer integrity
comments: Computational screening identified promising scaffolds but requires experimental validation of functional effects on serotonin biosynthesis rate.

model_io.model: Tetrameric human TPH-II with allosteric A-D interface pocket

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ligand binding at the A-D allosteric interface stabilizes TPH-II tetramer formation
hypotheses.result: Supported: all candidates maintained compact conformations; L2 showed optimal binding energetics

title: Saponins induce lipid-dependent structural heterogeneity and modulate membrane organization in phospholipid bilayers
task: Characterize saponin-induced membrane reorganization in sterol-free lipid bilayers
key_results: Saponins reduce lipid phase-transition cooperativity and induce structural heterogeneity in PC membranes (pronounced lamellar disruption, reduced assembly size) but not in PE membranes; calcein release substantially greater from PC than PE liposomes
comments: The lipid-composition dependence of saponin effects challenges the sterol-only mechanistic model and suggests interfacial interactions govern membrane activity.
